events.description: CT, echocardiography and ECG confirmed mirrored anatomy without bronchiectasis or structural cardiac abnormality; done on admission day 2 (24/02/2024)

evidence.quote: The CT corroborated complete visceral inversion—trilobed left lung, bilobed right lung; heart and great vessels mirrored; liver and gallbladder on the left; stomach, spleen, and colonic splenic flexure on the right (Figure 1A,B).

The scan showed no bronchiectasis (a noted artifact was confirmed not to represent pathology). An echocardiogram confirmed dextrocardia in the absence of structural abnormalities. A concurrent electrocardiogram (ECG) demonstrated characteristic features of dextrocardia, including sinus rhythm at 102 bpm, right axis deviation, inverted P waves in lead I, and absent R‐wave progression.
These studies were performed on the patient's second day of admission, corresponding to the sixth day of symptom onset [24/02/2024].

events.description: Laboratory and serologic workup largely normal/non-reactive except mild ALT elevation

evidence.quote: Laboratory investigations revealed a normal leukocyte count (4900/μL) with a neutrophil predominance (71.6%). Liver function tests showed a mild elevation of alanine transaminase (ALT, 42.3 IU/L) with a normal aspartate transaminase (AST, 35.36 IU/L). The rest of the serologic workup was unremarkable, including normal renal function, electrolytes, and thyroid‐stimulating hormone (TSH). Inflammatory markers such as the erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) were within normal limits. Serology for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), antinuclear antibody (ANA), Venereal Disease Research Laboratory (VDRL), and hepatitis B and C was non‐reactive. Urinalysis was unremarkable.

events.description: Final diagnosis of isolated SIT with isolated late-onset asthma; Kartagener syndrome/PCD excluded and associated anomalies not found

evidence.quote: The absence of chronic sinusitis, bronchiectasis, otorrhea, infertility indicators, or ciliary dysfunction rendered Kartagener syndrome unlikely. The final diagnosis comprised SIT with isolated late‐onset asthma. Kartagener syndrome was excluded, given the lack of its classical triad of chronic sinusitis, bronchiectasis, and ciliary dysfunction.
CT confirmed isolated SIT with no additional anomalies

summary.text: A 45-year-old Ethiopian man with long-suspected but never formally diagnosed asthma used intermittent pharmacy inhalers and was not controlled despite adherence to SABA and low-dose ICS. He presented with five days of progressive dyspnea, nocturnal dry cough, chest tightness and low-grade fever, worsened after a health-center visit, and was referred for advanced care.

On admission he had BP 112/70 mmHg, pulse 104 bpm, respiratory rate 26/min and room-air SpO2 90%, with accessory muscle use, diffuse expiratory wheezes and a right-sided apical impulse; an acute moderate asthma exacerbation without signs of pneumonia was diagnosed. Oxygen, bronchodilators and corticosteroids resolved symptoms within 48 hours.

After stabilization (symptom day 6), a chest radiograph showed dextrocardia, a right-sided aortic arch and a right-sided gastric air bubble. He consented to CT, echocardiography and ECG, done on admission day 2 (24/02/2024): CT showed complete visceral inversion without bronchiectasis, echocardiography confirmed dextrocardia without structural abnormality, and ECG showed sinus rhythm 102 bpm with right axis deviation, inverted lead I P waves and absent R-wave progression.
Laboratory work-up was normal or non-reactive except a mildly elevated ALT (42.3 IU/L) and neutrophil predominance (71.6%).

The final diagnosis was isolated situs inversus totalis, incidentally discovered, with isolated late-onset asthma. Kartagener syndrome and PCD were judged excluded clinically (no chronic sinusitis, bronchiectasis, neonatal distress, chronic wet cough or infertility indicators); no structural heart disease, malrotation or splenic anomaly was found, and laevocardia was excluded.

He denied personal and family history of diabetes, hypertension, cardiac disease, hearing loss, neonatal complications, chronic productive cough and recurrent infections; he is married and has six healthy siblings. Annual spirometry was advised and he was educated about how mirrored anatomy may affect future procedures; he expressed relief and commitment to annual pulmonary monitoring. No completed follow-up result is reported.

ambiguities.description: b00021 says Kartagener syndrome "necessitates the triad of SIT, chronic sinusitis, and bronchiectasis—none of which were present". Read in context (b00016 defines the triad as chronic sinusitis, bronchiectasis and ciliary dysfunction and excludes Kartagener for lack of it; SIT is the confirmed final diagnosis), "none of which" refers to the Kartagener-defining features beyond SIT, i.e. the triad was not fulfilled. This is loose authorial wording, not a clinical conflict about SIT; no SIT-absent fact is recorded and the sentence is not used as negative evidence for SIT.
